by: session, after Adrian's third watch (16 Oct 2026): show the plan, highlight M/N, explain 2 -> log3 9 at the 2, show x(x-8) = 9, reject only after explaining why; Herbert Gross pace

beats.say: Solve log base three of X minus eight equals two minus log base three of X.
asks: What does log base 3 mean?

beats.say: Here is the plan. Get one log on each side, both with base three.
asks: Why one log on each side?

beats.say: Then the two logs match, so the insides must be equal.
asks: Why can we compare the insides?

beats.say: First, move minus log base three of X to the left side. It becomes plus log base three of X.
asks: Why does the minus become plus?

beats.say: Now look at the two on the right. To match the plan, it must become a log with base three.
asks: Why must 2 become a log?

beats.say: Log base three of three is one. So two is the same as two times log base three of three.
asks: Why is log base 3 of 3 equal to 1?

beats.say: Log base three of three is one, because three to the power one is three.
asks: Why is log base 3 of 3 equal to 1?

beats.say: Bring the two up as a power. Two log base three of three becomes log base three of three squared.
asks: Why can the 2 go up as a power?

beats.say: Three squared is nine. So two is log base three of nine.
asks: Why is 2 = log base 3 of 9?

do.on: is log base three of nine

beats.say: Now join the two logs on the left with Add Power.
asks: What is Add Power?
Which law is this?

beats.say: Here M is X minus eight, and N is X.
asks: Which part is M and which is N?

beats.say: So we get log base three of X times X minus eight, equals log base three of nine.
asks: Why is it x times x minus 8?

beats.say: Now there is one log on each side, as planned. Look at the insides: X times X minus eight, and nine.
asks: Why can we drop the logs?

beats.say: The logs match, so the insides are equal. X times X minus eight equals nine.
asks: Why are the insides equal?

do.on: X times X minus eight equals

beats.say: Expand and bring nine across. X squared minus eight X minus nine equals zero.
asks: How do I expand x times x minus 8?

beats.say: Factorise. X minus nine, times X plus one, equals zero.
asks: How do I factorise this?

beats.say: So X equals nine, or X equals minus one.
asks: Why two answers?

beats.say: Now check each answer in the question. Put X equals minus one into log base three of X minus eight.
asks: Why must I check the answers?

beats.say: We get log base three of minus nine. That asks: three to what power gives minus nine.
asks: What does log base 3 of −9 mean?

beats.say: Three to any power is always positive. No power of three gives minus nine.
asks: Why is 3 to any power positive?

beats.say: So log base three of minus nine does not exist, and we reject X equals minus one.
asks: What does reject mean?

beats.say: X equals nine keeps both insides positive. The answer is X equals nine.
asks: How do I check x = 9?
